subject: Custodian Handover Workflow & Licensing Matrix for On-Prem Edge Deployments
messages:
From: Amanda Greene <amanda.greene@edgemed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Perez <mperez@procure.edgemed.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Custodian handover workflow & license matrix for on-prem edge deployments

Priyom —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our compliance team asked me to confirm two things before we proceed to signature for the Order Form:

1) How operator access will be limited during the snapshot/handback process for on-prem nodes (we need to avoid any remote write access to PHI-bearing data stores).
2) The exact license boundary if Redwood provides the runtime bundles and we ship a hardened appliance image. The attached Excel is our suggested licensing matrix (by component and operator role).

Can you review and confirm whether the proposed matrix maps to Redwood's standard private-deploy annex, or whether we need an addendum that explicitly defines custody/escrow-like access for emergency recoveries? We will need a short runbook and timeline for any attestation/audit window.

Attachments: EdgeMed_License_Matrix_v1.xlsx

Happy to hop on a call if easier.

Best,
Amanda Greene
Sr. Procurement Manager — EdgeMed Systems
Amanda.GreenE@edgemed.com

EdgeMed Systems | Procurement & Compliance
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Greene <amanda.greene@edgemed.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custodian handover workflow & license matrix for on-prem edge deployments

Amanda —

Thanks for the clear matrix. I reviewed with Chloe (solutions) and David (legal). High level response: Redwood can support the appliance model you described with a narrow operator boundary and an escrow-lite path for disaster recovery.

Key points:
- Operator access: we will supply an operator role with read-only runtime telemetry and maintenance logs by default. Any write or console-level operations require a documented, time-boxed escalation that is approved by EdgeMed and executed under a two-person control (Redwood engineer + EdgeMed ops).
- Evidence & attestation: we can provide a quarterly attestation package (logs, snapshot checksums, and a signed access audit) during the first 12 months post-deploy.
- Licensing boundary: propose we add an Order Form clause that enumerates components licensed (runtime, models, config tooling) and excludes customer data stores and local integrations.

I've attached a draft of our suggested redlines for the MSA annex and a short runbook outline (RI_Draft_Redlines.docx). Please review and we'll iterate. If you prefer, we can convert the licensing matrix table into a formal annex for signature.

Proposed next steps:
1) EdgeMed to confirm which operator actions (from your matrix) must remain prohibited absent a joint approval.
2) Redwood legal (David) to provide targeted redlines for the MSA/addendum.
3) Agree a 30-minute call on Thursday to walk the runbook and lock timelines for attestation delivery.

Attachments: RI_Draft_Redlines.docx

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Greene <amanda.greene@edgemed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custodian handover workflow & license matrix for on-prem edge deployments

Amanda / Priyom —

I reviewed the matrix and drafted targeted redlines for the MSA annex focused on: scope of licensed binaries, operator activity matrix, audit windows, and emergency recovery access. Two practical suggestions:

1) Emergency recovery escrow-lite: instead of full source escrow, we propose a controlled-access snapshot + signing key escrow (time-limited console session) where Redwood provides a signed token allowing a single recovery operation. Token issuance requires: (a) written EdgeMed approval, (b) two Redwood approvers, (c) an agreed maintenance window not exceeding 8 hours. After the operation, Redwood will deliver an access report and hash-matched snapshot evidence.

2) Evidence classification: add a table to the annex that labels evidence types (logs, checksums, config diff) and retention (90 days by default; extendable by request). This keeps the ask scoped and auditable.

I've included redline snippets in the attached DOCX. Operationally, Chloe and Priyom should confirm which matrix rows map to "no remote write" and which require joint ops approval.

Minor legal notes: we will not accept unconditional operator write privileges. We can accept time-limited, auditable access paired with an indemnity carveout for intentional misuse.

If this approach looks acceptable, I can prepare a short-form addendum (one page) that fits into your Order Form flow.

Attachments: RI_Draft_Redlines.docx

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference | Legal & Compliance
From: Amanda Greene <amanda.greene@edgemed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Perez <mperez@procure.edgemed.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custodian handover workflow & license matrix for on-prem edge deployments

Priyom / David —

Thanks, the approach makes sense and aligns with our security team’s appetite. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security:

- The tokenized recovery flow is acceptable provided EdgeMed can witness/approve the session and we get the signed access report within 48 hours.
- For the evidence retention: we will request 180 days for checksums/logs during the first year; can you confirm whether Redwood can extend retention to 180 days for EDG-2147 (we can accept a small fee if needed).
- Order Form: procurement wants the MSA addendum called out on the first page of the Order Form and would like the commercial term for the addendum (if any) to be explicit. Mike (cc’d) will handle the signature routing.

We are happy to sign the short-form addendum if Redwood adds the token workflow language and the 180-day retention option. Can we lock the language today so Mike can process the Order Form?

Regards,
Amanda Greene
Sr. Procurement Manager — EdgeMed Systems
